title: “The Short Dark Tetrad questionnaire”: A Russian adaptation in light of the general factor hypothesis
abstract: Context and relevance. This article presents a Russian adaptation of the Short Dark Tetrad (SD4) methodology, alternative to previously published by Kornienko et al. (2022). The instrument expands the Dark Triad concept by including a fourth factor — everyday sadism. Addressing the question of the independence of dark traits, various approaches to their conceptualization and diagnostics are analyzed: despite discrepancies between models, all directions indicate a pronounced overlap of these constructs and the existence of a common foundation or core. Methods and materials. The study involved 826 participants aged 18 to 63 years (M = 36.58; SD = 9.82; 77% women) and, in addition to the SD4, utilized the Dark Factor (D70) instrument to assess individual traits as manifestations of a general dark factor, as well as the Mini-IPIP for the Big Five. Results. Confirmatory factor analysis demonstrated satisfactory internal consistency and reliability. Results consistent with the literature were obtained: narcissism is positively associated with extraversion and openness, sadism negatively correlates with agreeableness; men exhibit higher scores on all scales except narcissism. The observed negative association of Machiavellianism with openness requires additional empirical verification due to discrepancies in existing research. Conclusions. Despite moderate correlations between similar scales across different instruments, contradictory patterns of interrelationships between scales were found. The necessity for a deeper analysis of theoretical and operational differences in dark trait models is discussed, especially considering existing contradictions in the literature.
